   579→```
   580→
   581→**Update (config only — same image, new revision with all secrets and env vars):**
   582→
   583→Use this to fix a revision that’s missing secrets (e.g. after an accidental `--set-secrets` that wiped others) or to set the full config in one shot.
   584→
   585→```bash
   586→# Minimal (required only). Add GOOGLE_API_KEY and OMOP_VOCAB_URL to --set-secrets if you use them.
   587→gcloud run services update api --region $REGION \

   592→With **Gemini + OMOP** (include every secret you use; `--set-secrets` replaces the whole map):
   593→
   594→```bash
   595→gcloud run services update api --region $REGION \
   596→  --set-env-vars "ENVIRONMENT=production,GCP_PROJECT_ID=${PROJECT_ID},GCP_REGION=${REGION},MODEL_BACKEND=vertex,VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID=${VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID},GCS_BUCKET_NAME=${GCS_BUCKET_NAME},USE_LOCAL_STORAGE=0,CORS_ORIGINS=${CORS_ORIGINS},GEMINI_MODEL_NAME=gemini-2.5-flash" \
   597→  --set-secrets "DATABASE_URL=db-url:latest,SESSION_SECRET=api-session-secret:latest,JWT_SECRET_KEY=api-jwt-secret:latest,GOOGLE_API_KEY=google-api-key:latest,OMOP_VOCAB_URL=omop-vocab-url:latest"
   598→```
   599→
   600→- **Secrets:** `--set-secrets` replaces the entire secret map. List every secret the API should have (required: `DATABASE_URL`, `SESSION_SECRET`, `JWT_SECRET_KEY`; optional: `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `OMOP_VOCAB_URL`). Omit optional ones if you don’t use them.
   601→- **Env vars:** `--set-env-vars` replaces all env vars. Add optional keys (e.g. `UMLS_API_KEY`, `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`) to the comma-separated list as needed.
   602→
   603→### 4.5 IAM: API service account (Cloud SQL, Vertex, Secret Manager)
   604→
   605→Cloud Run uses the default compute service account. Get its email and grant roles:
   606→
   607→```bash
   608→export PROJECT_NUMBER=$(gcloud projects describe $PROJECT_ID --format='value(projectNumber)')
   609→export API_SA="${PROJECT_NUMBER}-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com"
   610→```
   611→
   612→Grant:
   613→
   614→- **Cloud SQL Client** (connect to Cloud SQL)
   615→- **Vertex AI User** (call Vertex endpoint)
   616→- **Secret Manager Secret Accessor** (read DATABASE_URL, SESSION_SECRET, JWT_SECRET_KEY, and optionally GOOGLE_API_KEY; see 4.4a)
   617→- **Storage Object Admin** on the GCS bucket you use for protocol storage (see 4.6) — or `roles/storage.objectAdmin` at project level if you prefer.
   618→
   619→```bash
   620→for role in roles/cloudsql.client roles/aiplatform.user roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor; do
   621→  gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID \
   622→    --member="serviceAccount:${API_SA}" \
   623→    --role="$role"
   624→done
   625→```
   626→
   627→If you use a dedicated GCS bucket (recommended), grant the API SA access to that bucket only (do this after creating the bucket in 4.6):
   628→
   629→```bash
   630→gsutil iam ch serviceAccount:${API_SA}:objectAdmin gs://YOUR_BUCKET_NAME
   631→```
   632→
   633→If you use a **custom service account** for the API, use that email instead of `API_SA` and attach it with `--service-account=${API_SA}` in `gcloud run deploy api`.
   634→
   635→**Access control:** If you do not add `allUsers` as run.invoker (and do not use `--no-invoker-iam-check`), the API is **private**: only identities that you grant `roles/run.invoker` to can call it. You control access by adding or removing that role for users, groups, or service accounts.
   636→
   637→**If you get "Forbidden - Your client does not have permission to get URL"** when opening the API URL or `/docs`: the service is not allowing unauthenticated callers.
   638→
   639→- **If your project allows public access:** grant the public invoker role:  
   640→  `gcloud run services add-iam-policy-binding api --region=$REGION --member=allUsers --role=roles/run.invoker`
   641→
   642→- **If org policy blocks `allUsers`** ("users named in the policy do not belong to a permitted customer"): you cannot make the service public. Grant **run.invoker** to specific users or a group, then call the API with an identity token. Example for a user:
   643→
   644→  ```bash
   645→  # Grant your user (or a group) permission to invoke the service
   646→  gcloud run services add-iam-policy-binding api --region=$REGION \
   647→    --member="user:your-email@your-domain.com" \
   648→    --role=roles/run.invoker
   649→  ```
   650→
   651→  To call the API or open `/docs` (e.g. from curl), send an identity token:
   652→
   653→  ```bash
   654→  # Get a token and call the API (use your API URL)
   655→  TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-identity-token)
   656→  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://YOUR-API-URL.run.app/health
   657→  ```
   658→
   659→### 4.6 Make GCS and OMOP vocabulary available
   660→
   661→**Why the API needs a bucket**  
   662→The API uses a GCS bucket to store **protocol PDFs** (trial protocols uploaded by users). Flow: the frontend calls `POST /protocols/upload`, the API returns a **signed upload URL** so the browser uploads the PDF directly to GCS; the API stores the object path (`gs://bucket/protocols/...`) in the database. Later, extraction and review use that path, and the API issues **signed download URLs** when users open a protocol. Without a bucket (and without `USE_LOCAL_STORAGE=1`), upload and download of protocol files do not work in production.
   663→
   664→The `/health` endpoint reports **gcs** and **omop_vocab** as well as the main database. To get **everything available** (`"database":"connected"`, `"omop_vocab":"ok"`, `"gcs":"ok"`):
   665→
   666→| Order | What | Section / step below |
   667→|-------|------|----------------------|
   668→| 1 | Create GCS bucket + grant API SA access | **4.3a** (before API deploy) |
   669→| 2 | Deploy API (includes `GCS_BUCKET_NAME` and `USE_LOCAL_STORAGE=0`) | 4.4 |
   670→| 3 | Ensure OMOP database exists and is filled | Section 2.3–2.5 |
   671→| 4 | Update the API with `OMOP_VOCAB_URL` | OMOP vocabulary below; one-shot update |
   672→
   673→**GCS (protocol storage)**  
   674→Bucket creation and IAM are done in **section 4.3a** before the first API deploy. The deploy command in **4.4** already sets `GCS_BUCKET_NAME` and `USE_LOCAL_STORAGE=0`, so after deploy the API uses the bucket and health reports `"gcs": "ok"`.
   675→
   676→If you deployed the API without 4.3a, create the bucket and grant access (same commands as in 4.3a), then update the revision:
   677→
   678→```bash
   679→export GCS_BUCKET_NAME="${GCS_BUCKET_NAME:-${PROJECT_ID}-api-protocols}"
   680→gsutil mb -l $REGION gs://${GCS_BUCKET_NAME}
   681→gsutil iam ch serviceAccount:${API_SA}:objectAdmin gs://${GCS_BUCKET_NAME}
   682→gcloud run services update api --region $REGION \
   683→  --set-env-vars "GCS_BUCKET_NAME=${GCS_BUCKET_NAME},USE_LOCAL_STORAGE=0"
   684→```
   685→
   686→**OMOP vocabulary**
   687→
   688→The API expects a PostgreSQL database with the OMOP CDM vocabulary schema and at least the `concept` table populated. If you followed **section 2.3–2.5**, you already created the `omop_vocab` database on your Cloud SQL instance and filled it; set the URL when deploying or updating the API.
   689→
   690→- **Option A — Env var:** Set `OMOP_VOCAB_URL` (password will be visible in Cloud Run env). Use the same `CONNECTION_NAME`, `DB_USER`, and the **actual** DB password (e.g. from Secret Manager):
   691→
   692→  ```bash
   693→  export DB_PASSWORD=$(gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=db-password)
   694→  export OMOP_VOCAB_URL="postgresql://${DB_USER}:${DB_PASSWORD}@/omop_vocab?host=/cloudsql/${CONNECTION_NAME}"
   695→  gcloud run services update api --region $REGION \
   696→    --set-env-vars "OMOP_VOCAB_URL=${OMOP_VOCAB_URL}"
   697→  ```
   698→
   699→- **Option B — Secret (recommended):** Store the full URL in Secret Manager so the password is not in env:
   700→
   701→  ```bash
   702→  export DB_PASSWORD=$(gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=db-password)
   703→  export OMOP_VOCAB_URL="postgresql://${DB_USER}:${DB_PASSWORD}@/omop_vocab?host=/cloudsql/${CONNECTION_NAME}"
   704→  echo -n "$OMOP_VOCAB_URL" | gcloud secrets create omop-vocab-url --data-file=-
   705→  # If secret already exists: echo -n "$OMOP_VOCAB_URL" | gcloud secrets versions add omop-vocab-url --data-file=-
   706→  gcloud run services update api --region $REGION \
   707→    --set-secrets "OMOP_VOCAB_URL=omop-vocab-url:latest"
   708→  ```
   709→
   710→After OMOP is loaded and the URL is set, health will report `"omop_vocab": "ok"` (and optionally `omop_concept_count`). The **readiness** probe (`/ready`) requires OMOP to be available.
   711→
   712→**One-shot update (OMOP only)**
   713→
   714→Once the `omop_vocab` database is filled (section 2.3–2.5):
   715→
   716→1. Store OMOP URL in Secret Manager (if not already):  
   717→   `export DB_PASSWORD=$(gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=db-password)`  
   718→   `export OMOP_VOCAB_URL="postgresql://${DB_USER}:${DB_PASSWORD}@/omop_vocab?host=/cloudsql/${CONNECTION_NAME}"`  
   719→   Then either `echo -n "$OMOP_VOCAB_URL" | gcloud secrets create omop-vocab-url --data-file=-` or, if the secret exists, `echo -n "$OMOP_VOCAB_URL" | gcloud secrets versions add omop-vocab-url --data-file=-`.
   720→
   721→2. Update the API revision with OMOP (GCS is already set from 4.3a + 4.4):
   722→
   723→   ```bash
   724→   gcloud run services update api --region $REGION \
   725→     --set-secrets "OMOP_VOCAB_URL=omop-vocab-url:latest"
   726→   ```
   727→
   728→Then re-check `/health`: you should see `"omop_vocab":"ok"` and `"gcs":"ok"` (GCS was configured at deploy).
   729→
   730→### 4.6a Deploy MLflow tracking server (optional)
   731→
   732→The API can send experiment/trace data to an MLflow tracking server when `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` is set. The **simplest** way is to run MLflow on Cloud Run, using your existing **Cloud SQL** for metadata and **GCS** for artifacts. The backend store URI is stored in Secret Manager (no DB password in env).
   733→
   734→**1. Create MLflow database and artifact location**
   735→
   736→On your existing Cloud SQL instance, create a database for MLflow and a GCS path for artifacts:
   737→
   738→```bash
   739→# Reuse CONNECTION_NAME, INSTANCE_NAME, DB_USER from section 2
   740→gcloud sql databases create mlflow --instance=$INSTANCE_NAME
   741→
   742→# GCS bucket for MLflow artifacts
   743→export MLFLOW_ARTIFACT_BUCKET="${MLFLOW_ARTIFACT_BUCKET:-${PROJECT_ID}-mlflow-artifacts}"
   744→gsutil mb -l $REGION gs://${MLFLOW_ARTIFACT_BUCKET} 2>/dev/null || true
   745→# Grant the default compute SA (same as API) access so MLflow on Cloud Run can write
   746→export PROJECT_NUMBER=$(gcloud projects describe $PROJECT_ID --format='value(projectNumber)')
   747→gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding gs://${MLFLOW_ARTIFACT_BUCKET} \
   748→  --member="serviceAccount:${PROJECT_NUMBER}-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com" \
   749→  --role="roles/storage.objectAdmin"
   750→```
   751→
   752→**2. Store the MLflow backend store URI in Secret Manager**
   753→
   754→Build the Postgres URL for the `mlflow` database using the **DB password from Secret Manager**, then create a secret so the password is never in env or deploy commands:
   755→
   756→```bash
   757→# DB password from the same secret you use for the API (e.g. db-password or from db-url)
   758→export DB_PASSWORD=$(gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=db-password)
   759→# Backend: Postgres on Cloud SQL (same instance, database "mlflow")
   760→export MLFLOW_BACKEND_URI="postgresql://${DB_USER}:${DB_PASSWORD}@/mlflow?host=/cloudsql/${CONNECTION_NAME}"
   761→echo -n "$MLFLOW_BACKEND_URI" | gcloud secrets create mlflow-backend-uri --data-file=-
   762→# If the secret already exists (e.g. you're re-running): add a new version
   763→# echo -n "$MLFLOW_BACKEND_URI" | gcloud secrets versions add mlflow-backend-uri --data-file=-
   764→```
   765→
   766→Ensure the Cloud Run default compute service account can read this secret (it can if you already granted **Secret Manager Secret Accessor** in section 4.5 for the API).
   767→
   768→**3. Build and push the MLflow image**
   769→
   770→From the repo root:
   771→
   772→```bash
   773→gcloud builds submit --config=cloudbuild-mlflow.yaml --substitutions=_REGION=${REGION} .
   774→```
   775→
   776→**4. Deploy MLflow to Cloud Run**
   777→
   778→Inject the backend store URI from the secret; pass the artifact root as env (not sensitive):
   779→
   780→```bash
   781→export MLFLOW_ARTIFACT_ROOT="gs://${MLFLOW_ARTIFACT_BUCKET}/artifacts"
   782→
   783→gcloud run deploy mlflow \
   784→  --image ${REGION}-docker.pkg.dev/${PROJECT_ID}/app-images/mlflow:latest \
   785→  --region $REGION \
   786→  --platform managed \
   787→  --allow-unauthenticated \
   788→  --add-cloudsql-instances $CONNECTION_NAME \
   789→  --set-env-vars "MLFLOW_DEFAULT_ARTIFACT_ROOT=${MLFLOW_ARTIFACT_ROOT}" \
   790→  --set-secrets "REDACTED:latest"
   791→```
   792→
   793→**If the MLflow deployment fails,** check logs:
   794→
   795→```bash
   796→gcloud run services logs read mlflow --region $REGION --limit 200
   797→```
   798→
   799→Or in **Logging → Logs Explorer**: `resource.type="cloud_run_revision"` and `resource.labels.service_name="mlflow"`. Look for Python tracebacks, database connection errors, or Secret Manager permission errors.
   800→
   801→**5. Point the API at MLflow**
   802→
   803→After deploy, set the tracking URI on the API:
   804→
   805→```bash
   806→export MLFLOW_URL=$(gcloud run services describe mlflow --region $REGION --format='value(status.url)')
   807→gcloud run services update api --region $REGION \
   808→  --update-env-vars "MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=${MLFLOW_URL}"
   809→```
   810→
   811→The API will then log runs/traces to MLflow when `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` is set (e.g. LangChain autolog for extraction/grounding).
   812→
   813→**If you don’t have a `db-password` secret:** Use the same credentials you used to create `db-url` (section 2). You can create a dedicated secret: `echo -n "YOUR_DB_PASSWORD" | gcloud secrets create db-password --data-file=-`, or temporarily set `DB_PASSWORD` when building the URI and creating `mlflow-backend-uri` (the password is only in the secret after that).
   814→
   815→**Summary**
   816→
   817→| Step | Command / action |
   818→|------|------------------|
   819→| DB + GCS | Create DB `mlflow`, bucket, grant default compute SA `objectAdmin` on bucket |
   820→| Secret | Get `DB_PASSWORD` from Secret Manager; build Postgres URL for `mlflow` DB; create secret `mlflow-backend-uri` |
   821→| Build | `gcloud builds submit --config=cloudbuild-mlflow.yaml .` |
   822→| Deploy | `gcloud run deploy mlflow` with `--set-secrets "REDACTED:latest"` and `--set-env-vars "MLFLOW_DEFAULT_ARTIFACT_ROOT=gs://..."` |
   823→| API | `gcloud run services update api --update-env-vars "MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=<mlflow-url>"` |
   824→
   825→### 4.7 Update CORS after frontend URL is known
   826→
   827→After deploying the frontend (section 5), set CORS to the frontend origin:
   828→
   829→```bash
   830→export FRONTEND_URL="https://frontend-XXXXX-${REGION}.a.run.app"
   831→gcloud run services update api --region $REGION \
   832→  --set-env-vars "CORS_ORIGINS=${FRONTEND_URL}"
   833→```
   834→
   835→### 4.8 Updating the existing deployment
   836→
   837→After the API is deployed once, use the following to update it.
   838→
   839→**Code or image change (new build)**
   840→
   841→1. Rebuild and push the image (same as 4.2):
   842→
   843→   ```bash
   844→   cd /path/to/medgemma-hackathon-main
   845→   gcloud builds submit --config=cloudbuild-api.yaml --substitutions=_REGION=${REGION} .
   846→   ```
   847→
   848→2. Deploy the new image with the same config as 4.4. **For a single command that includes all secrets and env vars**, use the deploy block in **section 4.4b** (set `REGION`, `PROJECT_ID`, `CONNECTION_NAME`, `GCS_BUCKET_NAME`, `VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID`, `CORS_ORIGINS`, then run the deploy command there).
   849→
   850→**Env vars or secrets only (no new image)**
   851→
   852→Use `gcloud run services update api` so Cloud Run creates a new revision with updated config but the same image. **To set the full set of secrets and env vars in one command**, use the update block in **section 4.4b**.
   853→
   854→To change only one or two values without replacing everything:
   855→
   856→```bash
   857→# Add/update a single secret (keeps other secrets)
   858→gcloud run services update api --region $REGION --update-secrets "GOOGLE_API_KEY=google-api-key:latest"
   859→
   860→# Add/update env vars (merge with existing)
   861→gcloud run services update api --region $REGION --update-env-vars "CORS_ORIGINS=https://frontend-xxx.run.app,GEMINI_MODEL_NAME=gemini-2.5-flash"
   862→```
   863→
   864→- `--set-env-vars` replaces all env vars with the ones you list (include every var the service needs).
   865→- `--update-env-vars` adds or updates only the given keys; other env vars are unchanged.
   866→- `--set-secrets` / `--update-secrets` work the same way for secrets.
   867→
   868→After any update, the new revision serves traffic. Check `/health` to confirm.

   872→## 5. Deploy the Frontend to Cloud Run
   873→
   874→The frontend is a static SPA (Vite + React) built into a Docker image and served with Nginx. It needs the **API base URL at build time** (`VITE_API_URL`).
   875→
   876→### 5.1 Build and push the frontend image
   877→
   878→The frontend Dockerfile accepts build args `VITE_API_URL` and `BASE_PATH`. The API URL is baked into the static assets at build time.
   879→
   880→**Option A: Cloud Build** (recommended; no local Docker needed)
   881→
   882→Use the repo’s `cloudbuild-frontend.yaml`, which passes build args via substitutions. From the **repository root**:
   883→
   884→```bash
   885→# Set to your API Cloud Run URL (from step 4.4)
   886→export API_SERVICE_URL="https://api-XXXXX-${REGION}.a.run.app"
   887→
   888→gcloud builds submit \
   889→  --config=cloudbuild-frontend.yaml \
   890→  --substitutions=_VITE_API_URL="${API_SERVICE_URL}",_BASE_PATH="/",_REGION="${REGION}" \
   891→  .
   892→```
   893→
   894→**Option B: Local Docker**
   895→
   896→```bash
   897→export API_SERVICE_URL="https://api-XXXXX-${REGION}.a.run.app"
   898→
   899→docker build -f apps/hitl-ui/Dockerfile \
   900→  --build-arg VITE_API_URL="${API_SERVICE_URL}" \
   901→  --build-arg BASE_PATH="/" \
   902→  -t ${REGION}-docker.pkg.dev/${PROJECT_ID}/app-images/frontend:latest \
   903→  .
   904→
   905→docker push ${REGION}-docker.pkg.dev/${PROJECT_ID}/app-images/frontend:latest
   906→```
   907→
   908→Configure Docker for Artifact Registry auth if needed: `gcloud auth configure-docker ${REGION}-docker.pkg.dev`.
   909→
   910→### 5.2 Deploy the frontend service
   911→
   912→The frontend does not need secrets or Cloud SQL. It only needs to be reachable by users; it calls the API from the browser (using the URL baked in at build time).
   913→
   914→```bash
   915→gcloud run deploy frontend \
   916→  --image ${REGION}-docker.pkg.dev/${PROJECT_ID}/app-images/frontend:latest \
   917→  --region $REGION \
   918→  --platform managed \
   919→  --allow-unauthenticated
   920→```
   921→
   922→Cloud Run will serve the container; the default port the Dockerfile exposes is **8080**, which matches Cloud Run’s default.
   923→
   924→### 5.3 Make the frontend public (allow unauthenticated access)
   925→
   926→To let anyone open the frontend URL in a browser (no login), grant the public invoker role on the **frontend** service:
   927→
   928→```bash
   929→gcloud run services add-iam-policy-binding frontend \
   930→  --region=$REGION \
   931→  --member=allUsers \
   932→  --role=roles/run.invoker
   933→```
   934→
   935→If you used `--allow-unauthenticated` when you ran `gcloud run deploy frontend`, this binding may already exist. If you still get **Forbidden** when opening the frontend URL, run the command above explicitly.
   936→
   937→**If your org policy blocks `allUsers`** (error: "One or more users named in the policy do not belong to a permitted customer"):
   938→
   939→- **Option A — Grant invoker to specific users:**  
   940→  `gcloud run services add-iam-policy-binding frontend --region=$REGION --member="user:email@example.com" --role=roles/run.invoker`  
   941→  Access from a browser still requires an identity token. Use **Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP)** in front of the frontend (and optionally the API) so users sign in with Google and IAP forwards the token; or use a small proxy that adds the token.
   942→- **Option B — Host the frontend elsewhere:** Build the same static assets and serve them from **Firebase Hosting**, **Cloud Storage + Load Balancer**, or another host (Vercel, Netlify, etc.). Then the frontend URL is not Cloud Run and is not subject to Cloud Run IAM. Point `VITE_API_URL` at your API and set API CORS to the new frontend origin.
   943→- **Option C — Org admin:** See **Appendix: Allow public Cloud Run (for org admins)** below.
   944→
   945→### 5.4 Frontend IAM (service account)
   946→
   947→The frontend is a static site; it does not call GCP APIs from the server. It only needs to be **invokable by unauthenticated users** (or by your chosen identity if you restrict access). No extra IAM roles are required for the frontend service account for “reaching” the API: the browser calls the API URL directly, and CORS is configured on the API side (step 4.6).
   948→
   949→If you later add server-side API calls from the frontend container, you would grant the frontend’s service account only the roles needed for those calls.

   966→
   967→## 7. Summary: order of operations and permissions
   968→
   969→| Step | What | Notes |
   970→|------|------|--------|
   971→| 1 | Enable APIs, set project/region | One-time |
   972→| 2 | Create Cloud SQL instance, database, user; store password (and optionally full DATABASE_URL) in Secret Manager | Tiny instance: e.g. `db-f1-micro` |
   973→| 3 | Create Artifact Registry repo | One-time |
   974→| 4 | Build API image → push → deploy API to Cloud Run with Cloud SQL connection, env vars, secrets | Set CORS after frontend URL is known |
   975→| 4.5 | Grant API service account: Cloud SQL Client, Vertex AI User, Secret Manager Secret Accessor | So API can reach DB, Vertex, and secrets |
   976→| 5 | Build frontend image with `VITE_API_URL` = API Cloud Run URL → push → deploy frontend to Cloud Run | No extra IAM for “calling API”; browser uses API URL |
   977→| 6 | Update API CORS to frontend URL | So browser can call API from frontend origin |
   978→
   979→**Who calls what**
   980→
   981→- **Browser** → Frontend (Cloud Run) → static assets.  
   982→- **Browser** → API (Cloud Run) → API handles auth, DB, and triggers protocol processing.  
   983→- **API (Cloud Run)** → Cloud SQL (via Unix socket), Secret Manager, **Vertex AI endpoint** (MedGemma).  
   984→- Frontend does not need GCP IAM to “reach” the API; CORS on the API allows the frontend origin.

   990→**API (Cloud Run)** — For a single deploy/update command that sets all of these, see **section 4.4b**.
   991→
   992→- **Required**: `ENVIRONMENT=production`, `DATABASE_URL` (secret), `SESSION_SECRET` (secret), `JWT_SECRET_KEY` (secret).  
   993→- **Vertex**: `GCP_PROJECT_ID`, `GCP_REGION`, `MODEL_BACKEND=vertex`, `VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID` (or `VERTEX_MODEL_NAME`).  
   994→- **CORS**: `CORS_ORIGINS=https://your-frontend-url`.  
   995→- **Optional**: `GEMINI_MODEL_NAME` (env), `GOOGLE_API_KEY` (secret — see 4.4a for Gemini), `UMLS_API_KEY`, `OMOP_VOCAB_URL`, `GCS_BUCKET_NAME`, `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`, OAuth client id/secret.
   996→- **Health (omop_vocab + gcs available):** Set `GCS_BUCKET_NAME` and `USE_LOCAL_STORAGE=0`; set `OMOP_VOCAB_URL` (env or secret). Create bucket, grant API SA `objectAdmin` on it, fill OMOP DB (2.3–2.5). See **section 4.6**.
   997→
   998→**Frontend**
   999→
  1000→- **Build-time only**: `VITE_API_URL` (Cloud Run API URL), `BASE_PATH` (e.g. `/`). No runtime secrets required for basic deployment.
  1001→
  1002→**IAM (API service account)**
  1003→
  1004→- `roles/cloudsql.client`  
  1005→- `roles/aiplatform.user`  
  1006→- `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor`  
  1007→- GCS: `gsutil iam ch serviceAccount:${API_SA}:objectAdmin gs://YOUR_BUCKET_NAME` (or project-level `roles/storage.objectAdmin`)
  1008→
  1009→---
  1010→
  1011→## Appendix: Allow public Cloud Run (for org admins)
  1012→
  1013→When a developer runs:
  1014→
  1015→```bash
  1016→gcloud run services add-iam-policy-binding frontend --region=REGION --member=allUsers --role=roles/run.invoker
  1017→```
  1018→
  1019→and gets **"One or more users named in the policy do not belong to a permitted customer, perhaps due to an organization policy"**, an organization policy is blocking the use of `allUsers` (public access) on Cloud Run.
  1020→
  1021→**What the org admin needs to do**
  1022→
  1023→1. **Identify the policy**  
  1024→   In [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/) → **IAM & Admin** → **Organization policies** (or go to the **Resource Manager** and select the org/folder).  
  1025→   The constraint is usually one of:
  1026→   - **Domain restricted sharing** (`iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains`) — limits which principals (e.g. which domains) can be added to IAM policies; `allUsers` is not in any domain, so it is blocked.
  1027→   - A **custom org policy** that restricts “public” or “unauthenticated” access to certain resources.
  1028→
  1029→2. **Add an exception for the project (or for Cloud Run)**  
  1030→   - Open the policy that restricts public/allUsers (e.g. **Domain restricted sharing**).
  1031→   - **Edit** the policy.
  1032→   - Add a **rule** that applies only to the **project** (or folder) where the frontend/API run, and set it to **Allow** or **Replace** so that this project is **exempt** from the restriction.  
  1033→   - Or, if the policy has a list of allowed principals or conditions, add an exception that allows `allUsers` for the role `roles/run.invoker` on Cloud Run services in that project (syntax depends on the constraint).
  1034→
  1035→3. **Typical flow for “Domain restricted sharing”**  
  1036→   - Policy is set at **Organization** or **Folder** level.
  1037→   - Add a **policy exception** for the **project ID** where the developer deploys the frontend (and API).  
  1038→   - Exception type: “Allow” or “Replace” so the policy is not enforced on that project (or so `allUsers` is allowed for Cloud Run in that project).  
  1039→   - Save. After a few minutes, the developer can retry the `add-iam-policy-binding` command.
  1040→
  1041→4. **If the org does not allow exceptions**  
  1042→   The developer must use **Option A** (invoker for specific users + IAP or proxy) or **Option B** (host the frontend on Firebase Hosting, Vercel, etc.) from section 5.3.
  1043→
  1044→**References**
  1045→
  1046→- [Organization policy constraints](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/organization-policy/org-policy-constraints)  
  1047→- [Domain restricted sharing](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/organization-policy/restricting-domains)  
  1048→- [Cloud Run IAM](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/securing/managing-access)
  1049→

content.text:
Your GCP organization has a **Domain Restricted Sharing** policy that blocks `allUsers` (public access). This is common in enterprise GCP orgs.

You have two options:

**Option A: Use `allAuthenticatedUsers` instead** (allows any Google-signed-in user, not fully public):
```bash
gcloud run services add-iam-policy-binding api \
  --region=europe-west4 \
  --member="allAuthenticatedUsers" \
  --role="roles/run.invoker"
```

**Option B: Disable the org policy constraint** (requires Org Admin):
```bash
# Check which constraint is blocking:
gcloud org-policies describe constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains \
  --project=$(gcloud config get-value project)
```
Then an org admin can add an exception or remove the constraint.

**Option C: Use Cloud Run's built-in auth proxy** — set ingress to "Allow all" and use IAP (Identity-Aware Proxy) instead, which lets you control access at the Google level while still allowing browser traffic through.

I'd recommend trying **Option A** first — it should work with the org policy while still letting browser OAuth work since users will already be signed into Google.

You're right to be confused — the 403 isn't about *your* identity. Cloud Run's IAM auth check happens **before** your app receives the request. When IAM invoker auth is enabled, Cloud Run expects every incoming HTTP request to carry a valid GCP IAM token in the `Authorization` header. It's essentially a blanket "no unauthenticated HTTP requests allowed" gate, not a user-level check.

The fix is to disable that gate so traffic reaches your app, which handles its own auth. Let me try:

The error is `invalid_client`, not `access_denied` — this means Google can't find the client at all, not that you're unauthorized. But we proved via `curl` that the client/secret pair is valid.

This is likely a **Branding** issue. In the new Google Auth Platform, you need to complete the branding setup before the OAuth consent screen works in the browser. 

Click on **Branding** in the left sidebar — does it show any warnings or incomplete fields (app name, support email, etc.)? If the branding isn't fully configured, Google blocks the browser OAuth flow with `invalid_client` even though the client technically exists.
[Image: original 2286x1694, displayed at 2000x1482. Multiply coordinates by 1.14 to map to original image.]

Audience looks fine — you're a test user. The `invalid_client` error is puzzling since the client exists and the API-level test worked.

Since all your users are `@elixirtrials.com`, click **"Make internal"** — this restricts login to your org only and skips the "Testing" mode restrictions entirely. This is simpler and more secure for your use case.

If the `invalid_client` error persists after that, click on **Branding** and show me what's there — incomplete branding config is the other common cause of this error.
Must I fill in these:

content.text:
Found it! Look at the redirect URL:

```
client_id=None
```

The `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` env var is not being picked up by the `authlib` OAuth client. The issue is that `authlib` reads `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` at **registration time** (when `oauth.register()` runs at module import), but the env vars were set as Cloud Run env vars *after* the code was written. The `oauth.register()` call doesn't pass `client_id` explicitly — it relies on authlib's auto-discovery, which looks for specific env var names.

Let me check how authlib expects them:

content.text: That's the problem. `authlib` with Starlette looks for `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` env vars automatically, but the naming convention it expects is `{NAME}_CLIENT_ID` where `{NAME}` is the uppercase version of the `name` parameter. That should work... unless there's a version difference. Let me fix it explicitly:
